Mattaniah
mat-ta-nī'ä
n. (a Levite of the sons of Asaph who was the principal to begin the thanksgiving in prayer after the captivity; also the original name of king Zedekiah, and of several other men)
From Hebrew Mattanyah, gift of the LORD, from mattan, a gift, and the divine name Yah. It was the birth-name of Judah's last king: Nebuchadnezzar made Mattaniah king and changed his name to Zedekiah (2Ki 24:17), a heathen monarch renaming a son of David as an act of ownership.

Biblical Definition

Mattaniah is a name worn by singers, gatekeepers, penitents and one doomed king, and its most memorable bearer holds a post described in a single clause of great beauty: “And Mattaniah the son of Micha, the son of Zabdi, the son of Asaph, was the principal to begin the thanksgiving in prayer” (Neh 11:17). Somebody has to start. In a congregation newly returned from seventy years in Babylon, standing in a city with broken walls before a house that made the old men weep, one Levite of Asaph's line was appointed to lead off the praise. He is named again in the roll of the Levites who came up with Zerubbabel: “Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah, which was over the thanksgiving, he and his brethren” (Neh 12:8). The Chronicler traces the same family back into David's choir, where the ninth of the twenty-four courses fell to a Mattaniah of the sons of Heman (1Ch 25:16), and another Mattaniah of the sons of Asaph helped cleanse the house under Hezekiah (2Ch 29:13). A less happy Mattaniah appears in Ezra's list of those who had taken strange wives and put them away (Ezr 10:26). The thread through all of them is service in the house of God across five centuries, by men whose name means gift of the LORD.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no article for Mattaniah; in sacred history it is the name of several Levites and singers, and the original name of Zedekiah king of Judah.

MATTANIAH, n. Gift of the LORD; a proper name borne by several men in the Hebrew Scriptures.

A Levite of the sons of Asaph, the principal to begin the thanksgiving in prayer.

He was over the thanksgiving among the Levites who returned with Zerubbabel.

The ninth course of the singers in the days of David fell to a Mattaniah.

Mattaniah was also the name of the last king of Judah before Nebuchadnezzar called him Zedekiah.

Key Scripture

Neh 11:17 — "And Mattaniah the son of Micha, the son of Zabdi, the son of Asaph, was the principal to begin the thanksgiving in prayer: and Bakbukiah the second among his brethren, and Abda the son of Shammua, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun."

Neh 12:8 — "Moreover the Levites: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah, which was over the thanksgiving, he and his brethren."

1Ch 25:16 — "The ninth to Mattaniah, he, his sons, and his brethren, were twelve:"

2Ch 29:13 — "And of the sons of Elizaphan; Shimri, and Jeiel: and of the sons of Asaph; Zechariah, and Mattaniah:"

Modern Corruption

There is no significant modern redefinition of this name. The principle to recover is that thanksgiving in the assembly is an appointed office and a duty, not a mood that must be waited for.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Mattaniah is a Levite in a register and nobody has contested him. What his post sets against the modern congregation is the idea that praise is an ordered work. Nehemiah does not record that the people felt thankful; he records that a man was appointed to begin the thanksgiving in prayer, that he had brethren under him, that they were maintained by daily portions, and that the whole arrangement went back to the commandment of David the man of God. Thanksgiving in Scripture is a discipline with a rota attached.

The principle to recover is that duty leads and feeling follows. The psalms command it upon the soul rather than waiting on it: “Bless the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name” (Psa 103:1). Hebrews makes it a sacrifice offered continually: “By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name” (Heb 13:15). A church that will only sing when it is moved has confused worship with sentiment; the returned exiles, who had every reason for grief and sang anyway, understood the thing better. Somebody had to begin, and it was Mattaniah's job.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Mattanyah (H4983), gift of the LORD; mattan (H4976), gift; Yah (H3050), the LORD; todah (H8426), thanksgiving, thank-offering; ro'sh (H7218), head, chief, principal.

expand to see more

Hebrew Mattanyah (H4983) — Mattaniah; gift of the LORD.

Hebrew mattan (H4976) — a gift; the first element of the name.

Hebrew Yah (H3050) — the shortened divine name closing it.

Hebrew todah (H8426) — thanksgiving; the office he was set over.

Hebrew ro'sh (H7218) — chief; ‘the principal to begin’.

Usage

"“The principal to begin the thanksgiving in prayer” — an office nobody thinks to appoint today."

"“Which was over the thanksgiving, he and his brethren” — praise organised as a charge."

"“The ninth to Mattaniah” — a course of the singers under David."
